overview: The Medford City Council addressed business impacts from the Cradock Bridge construction project, zoning and tree preservation concerns at 0 Walnut Street, and approved a Class 4 auto body license and a housing authority appointment. The Council also passed multiple resolutions regarding public safety, sidewalk dumping, municipal maintenance, and requests for school and budget information.

items.title: National Drug Take Back Initiative Announcement
items.summary: President Dello Russo announced that the Medford Police Department and Board of Health will host the 11th National Drug Take Back Initiative on April 30, 2016.

items.title: 0 Walnut Street Buildable Lot and Tree Preservation Inquiry
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting building department updates, legal opinions, and arborist reports regarding zoning buildability and the preservation of a 125-year-old beech tree at 0 Walnut Street.

items.title: Cradock Bridge Construction Business Impacts and Mitigation
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting MassDOT and city officials address construction disruptions, vibration monitoring, window cleaning, parking restoration, and liaison communications for local businesses.

items.title: Roberts Elementary School Mural Announcement
items.summary: Cheryl Rodriguez invited the Council and public to attend the unveiling of a grant-funded school mural at Roberts Elementary School on May 26.

items.title: Public Hearing: Seiko Autobody Inc. Class 4 License
items.summary: Approved the application of Seiko Autobody Inc. for a Class 4 auto repair and body shop license at 391-397 Riverside Avenue.

items.title: Medford Housing Authority Appointment: Michael J. Lewis
items.summary: Confirmed the appointment of Michael J. Lewis to the Medford Housing Authority for a five-year term expiring April 8, 2021.

items.title: Subcommittee on Zoning and Ordinances Report
items.summary: Accepted the subcommittee report, placing two items on file and retaining two items in committee.

items.title: Commendations and Infrastructure Resolutions
items.summary: Approved several resolutions commending local resurfacing, hockey award recipient Bill Riley, and police and fire personnel for playground repairs, while requesting cleanup along Circuit Street, Clematis Road, and Woodruff Avenue.

items.title: Basketball Rim Replacement at Magoon Park
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting the Park Department immediately replace damaged basketball rims at Magoon Park.

items.title: Illegal Sidewalk Dumping and Code Enforcement Policy
items.summary: Approved a resolution advocating for a formal city policy, proactive code enforcement, and university accountability to prevent seasonal illegal dumping on sidewalks.

items.title: High Street Electronic Speed Sign Repair
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting repairs to the non-functioning electronic speed sign on High Street near the Brooks School.

items.title: School Department and Municipal Budget Inquiries
items.summary: Approved requests to be updated on potential external leasing of Edgley Field, receive a budget template from the administration, and obtain a copy of the Superintendent's contract.
